phases.title: Baseline Object Distance Estimation
phases.subtitle: Establish the foundation
phases.goal: Integrate 2D object bounding boxes (YOLOv11) with dense monocular depth maps (UniDAC) for metric distance estimation on real-world road scenes.
phases.technique: Gaussian-weighted spatial pooling over object masks with median scale calibration on KITTI-360. YOLO11 detects objects, UniDAC provides depth, and median-depth sampling inside each bounding box yields metric distances.
findings: Solid performance on rigid road objects (cars, pedestrians, cyclists)
Pipeline validated on standard automotive scenarios
Distance estimation within acceptable error bounds for highway driving
phases.outcome: Working baseline pipeline. Accurate for road scenes, but untested on optically complex environments.

phases.title: Discovery of Optical Failure Cases
phases.subtitle: When vision fails
phases.goal: Stress-test the baseline system on non-automotive, optically complex scenes to identify fundamental failure modes.
phases.technique: Systematic evaluation of baseline depth estimator on camouflage, transparent glass, and textureless scenes from diverse image sources.
findings: Camouflage: Animal boundaries blended completely into foliage — depth maps flat across animal-tree interfaces
Glass & Transparency: Wine glasses and beakers invisible in depth maps — estimator looked through to background
Textureless Walls: Smooth white rooms suffered severe spherical bulging and depth warping
evidence: Side-by-side RGB vs depth failure examples
phases.outcome: Defined the three target failure domains that DepthForge is designed to address.

phases.title: Multi-Domain Benchmark Assembly
phases.subtitle: Building the evaluation set
phases.goal: Construct a rigorous multi-domain evaluation benchmark using authentic images from established computer-vision datasets.
phases.technique: Curated images from COD10K (camouflage), GSD Glass Surface Detection dataset (glass), and NYU Depth v2 (textureless indoor). Applied scene-level grouping to prevent train/test leakage.
findings: COD10K provides diverse camouflage scenes with confirmed ground truth
GSD dataset contains real glass surfaces and dual-view pairs
NYU Depth v2 offers clean indoor/textureless depth references
problems: Initial dataset had unbalanced domain representation (95% camouflage)
evidence: Examples of depth bleeding and surface distortion
phases.outcome: Assembled 3-domain benchmark; initial imbalance identified as a problem to fix.

phases.title: Foundational Model Bake-Off
phases.subtitle: Choosing the right backbone
phases.goal: Systematically compare 5 major depth estimation architectures to select the optimal backbone and teacher model.
phases.technique: Evaluated MiDaS-Small, MiDaS-Hybrid, UniDAC (DINOv2+DPT), DPT-Large, and Depth Anything under comparable protocols on the 3-domain benchmark.
findings: MiDaS-Small (21M params): Fast ~30 FPS, heavily blurred high-frequency contours
MiDaS-Hybrid (68M params): Balanced, moderate edge recovery
UniDAC (DINOv2+DPT): Strong semantic reasoning, struggled on refractive boundaries
DPT-Large (345M params): Superb geometric fidelity, too heavy for real-time edge devices
problems: No single model solved all three domains well
phases.outcome: Selected MiDaS-Small as baseline (fast, trainable), DPT-Large as teacher pseudo-GT provider.

phases.title: Early Lightweight Adapters
phases.subtitle: First refinement attempts
phases.goal: Design a lightweight plug-in adapter that refines MiDaS-Small output without retraining the expensive backbone.
phases.technique: Edge-guided single-scale residual adapter. Input: [base depth || RGB || Sobel gradient]. Output: residual correction clamped via tanh gating.
findings: Residual adapter concept validated — small corrections can recover boundaries
Single-scale processing misses multi-resolution context
Sobel edge prior is a strong signal for boundary recovery
problems: Single dilation insufficient for both fine edges and regional geometry
phases.outcome: Proved adapter concept. Motivated multi-scale dilated design.

phases.title: Multi-Scale Dilated Architecture
phases.subtitle: Capturing edge and context
phases.goal: Extend the adapter with parallel dilated convolutions at multiple receptive fields to capture both fine edge transitions and wide surface context.
phases.technique: Parallel branches with dilations d={1,2,4} concatenated into 96-channel feature map. Tanh gating with alpha=0.30 for stable residual magnitude control.
findings: Multi-scale features improve both boundary sharpness and surface continuity
Dilation d=1 captures fine edge details, d=4 captures regional curvature context
Tanh gating prevents runaway residuals while allowing meaningful corrections
problems: Still a single-head design — same correction applied regardless of scene domain
phases.outcome: Multi-scale dilated trunk became the shared foundation for Phase 9's multi-head design.

phases.title: Comprehensive Diagnostic Audit
phases.subtitle: Exposing hidden flaws
phases.goal: Conduct a systematic audit of the evaluation pipeline to identify and correct methodological flaws before final reporting.
phases.technique: Manual review of loss functions, dataset splits, metric definitions, and training supervision sources.
findings: FLAW 1 — Self-Distillation Loop: Model supervised by its own base depth (circular bias, cannot generalize)
FLAW 2 — Flawed Metric (BSI): Boundary Smoothness Index rewarded high-frequency hallucinated noise
FLAW 3 — Class Imbalance: 95.8% camouflage vs only 4.2% glass/textureless in training data
FLAW 4 — Grid-Crop Data Leakage: Sub-crops of same photos in both train and test splits
problems: All previous metrics potentially contaminated by these four flaws
phases.outcome: Corrected protocol: cross-model supervision, SILog+Grad loss, balanced dataset, scene-level splits.

phases.title: Final Verified Pipeline
phases.subtitle: Clean experimental methodology
phases.goal: Re-run the full experiment with all audit corrections applied to establish a trustworthy performance baseline.
phases.technique: Cross-model DPT-Large pseudo-GT supervision. SILog + Gradient Consistency loss. Authentic 522-image balanced dataset. Zero-leakage scene-level partitioning. 40 epochs on GPU.
findings: AbsRel improved +13.3% overall vs baseline after correcting all flaws
Camouflage +13.5%, Glass -17.1% SILog error, Textureless +7.6%
Single-head adapter (83.4K params) achieved meaningful improvements under fair evaluation
problems: Single head architecture — cannot specialize per domain
phases.outcome: Clean benchmark. Motivated Phase 9: add domain-specialist heads and automated routing.

phases.title: Multi-Head Domain-Expert Adapter
phases.subtitle: Specialist experts + automatic routing
phases.goal: Introduce three domain-specialist expert heads with a learned soft domain router to replace the monolithic single-head design.
phases.technique: Shared multi-scale dilated trunk → three expert heads (camouflage, glass, textureless) → soft router blends expert residuals via learned domain weights → tanh gated residual addition.
findings: Overall AbsRel reduced +2.9% (0.5848 → 0.5680) across 450-image test set
Glass domain: +4.7% AbsRel improvement — dedicated expert resolves refraction ambiguity
Camouflage: +3.8% AbsRel improvement — crisp boundary separation recovered
94.4% routing accuracy (425/450) with zero test-time domain labels
Ultra-lightweight: 228,374 parameters (~857 KB) with <5ms GPU inference
problems: SILog slightly worsens (sharp edges vs smooth pseudo-GT divergence in log space)
phases.outcome: DepthForge Phase 9: production-ready multi-expert depth refinement with autonomous domain routing.
